about.bio: I am Skandar Hadrich, an ICT Engineering student at ENIT specializing in cybersecurity, low-level systems, and ML-for-security. My research centers on automated malware analysis, reverse engineering, and threat research using GNNs, RL, and eBPF. Most notably, I architected an 8-stage nested-VM malware analysis sandbox with live hypervisor eBPF tracing and Volatility3 VMI correlation. I hold 6 certifications—including NVIDIA LLM Fine-Tuning—and maintain a Top 1% global ranking on TryHackMe along with a #77 global HTB Uni CTF team finish. My engineering expertise spans SOC automation, DevSecOps pipelines, network intrusion detection, and binary disassembly. I am currently seeking a 6-month research internship starting early 2027 in systems security, binary analysis, or AI security.

fields.val: Malware Analysis · Reverse Engineering · Penetration Testing

bullets: Architected an end-to-end 9-stage automated malware analysis pipeline in five phases: static triage with a .NET/native fork, live KVM/QEMU detonation with concurrent eBPF, VMI and network telemetry, then IOC extraction, threat-intel pivoting, weighted scoring, MinHash/LSH clustering and MITRE ATT&CK mapping into an automated PDF report.

Correlated host-side eBPF KVM tracepoints with Volatility3 VMI on a live guest, and patched KUSER_SHARED_DATA.TickCount in guest memory to defeat anti-sandbox timing checks. Validated against live AsyncRAT, AgentTesla and njRAT samples.
Deployed a multi-layer C2 sinkhole (iptables + DNSChef + INetSim) to capture malware traffic and extract actionable IOCs with false-positive filtering against Windows telemetry.
Automated threat attribution by matching IOCs against VirusTotal, AlienVault OTX and MalwareBazaar, grouping behavioural families with MinHash LSH clustering and generating PDF reports automatically.
Triaged 15+ daily technical support tickets and provisioned network modems at scale, cutting average per-unit configuration time by 20% through scripted workflows.
Maintained network uptime across multiple customer sites.

projects.name: Nested-VM Malware Analysis Pipeline
projects.desc: An end-to-end 9-stage automated malware analysis pipeline in five phases. QEMU/KVM live detonation with host-side eBPF syscall tracing correlated against Volatility3 VMI, anti-sandbox evasion via KUSER_SHARED_DATA patching in guest memory, multi-layer C2 sinkholing with DNSChef + INetSim + iptables, and automated MITRE ATT&CK attribution with MinHash LSH clustering. Validated against live AsyncRAT, AgentTesla and njRAT samples.

projects.name: CFG Function Localization via Graph Neural Networks
projects.desc: Stripped ELF/PE binaries disassembled with headless Ghidra and angr, then mapped into directed control-flow graphs whose node features are x86/ARM opcode distributions and API call references. GCNs and GATs (PyTorch Geometric) are trained for node-level classification of malicious functions — anti-debug loops, keyloggers and process-injection routines.

projects.name: RL-Based Intrusion Detection & Response
projects.desc: Network defense formulated as an MDP with six response actions (DPI, throttle, honeypot, block, isolate, quarantine) inside a custom Gymnasium environment. A Double DQN agent with prioritized experience replay is trained on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 telemetry to choose response actions instead of only raising alerts.

projects.name: Open-Source SOC Automation
projects.desc: A Wazuh SIEM + Shuffle SOAR lab deployed automatically with Ansible and Docker. A Python suppression microservice filters 33,022 noisy events down to a single actionable incident — over 95% noise reduction — with a human-in-the-loop VirusTotal enrichment pipeline and custom detection rules validated against simulated brute force, lateral movement and privilege escalation.

projects.name: Wi-Fi Security Research
projects.desc: Demonstrated WPA2 and ARP-spoofing weaknesses with Wireshark and Bettercap in an isolated lab. Documented the MITM attack chain end to end and proposed concrete mitigations: 802.1X, HSTS enforcement and certificate pinning.

projects.name: Village Under Attack — C++ Strategy Game
projects.desc: A real-time terminal strategy game in C++ built on OOP principles, non-blocking I/O, NPC pathfinding and collision detection. Systems programming and algorithmic design outside a security context — the discipline that makes the reversing work easier.

projects.name: Embedded Face Recognition & Hardware Automation
projects.desc: A real-time facial recognition pipeline in Python/OpenCV driving an Arduino microcontroller over UART. Identity verification triggers a physical hardware action, demonstrating secure serial protocol design and embedded security.

phases.name: Pre-detonation triage & static analysis
phases.blurb: Nothing executes yet. The orchestrator triages the sample, forks it into a managed or a native path, and both converge on a decision about what — if anything — is safe to detonate.
phases.aside: A .NET verdict routes the sample to 2b; a native one falls through 2 → 3 → 4. Both paths end at detonation target determination, which chooses the extracted payload or falls back to the original binary.

stages.name: Static triage
stages.note: Hashes, entropy, PE/ELF headers, digital signatures — first verdict and risk score

stages.name: Generic deobfuscation
stages.note: Stack-string decoding, XOR/Base64/RC4 decryption, regex IoC extraction

stages.name: .NET unpacking
stages.note: CLR header validation, de4dot unpacking, timing-patch injection, embedded C2 strings

stages.name: CFG extraction
stages.note: Control-flow graph via angr, cyclomatic complexity, obfuscation scoring

stages.name: User-mode emulation
stages.note: Conditional Windows API emulation and in-memory payload extraction

phases.name: Live detonation & concurrent telemetry
phases.blurb: The dynamic window. CleanState restore, uptime-evasion patching, three monitoring engines and a network tap, all writing into one master timeline.
phases.aside: INetSim, DNSChef and iptables stand up network deception and redirect every C2 call to the sinkhole on port 4444.

stages.name: Snapshot & evasion
stages.note: CleanState restore, then KUSER_SHARED_DATA.TickCount is patched to defeat GetTickCount-based uptime checks

stages.name: eBPF monitor
stages.note: Host-context syscalls and socket operations from KVM tracepoints

stages.name: VMI process tree
stages.note: Guest process creation, injection and termination via libVMI / Volatility 3

stages.name: Network TAP
stages.note: Virtual-NIC frame capture on virbr1

stages.name: Timeline correlation
stages.note: eBPF and VMI events merged into master_timeline.json for the whole run

phases.name: Post-detonation enrichment & scoring
phases.blurb: Once the window closes the evidence is normalised, enriched against outside threat intel, and folded into a single weighted score.

stages.name: Config decryption
stages.note: Family-specific config decryption for NjRAT, AsyncRAT and AgentTesla

stages.name: IOC extraction
stages.note: RFC-compliant normalisation and OS-telemetry noise filtering → validated_iocs.json

stages.name: Threat-intel pivot
stages.note: VirusTotal, AlienVault OTX and MalwareBazaar hits, correlated against INetSim DNS logs

stages.name: Scoring
stages.note: Every artefact aggregated into a unified weighted risk score and verdict

phases.name: Master merge, clustering & ATT&CK mapping
phases.blurb: The run is compared against every previous run in the workspace, then enriched into the report skeleton.
phases.aside: Cluster similarity feeds a second scoring pass before the report is sealed as master_report_<sha256>.json.

stages.name: Behavioural clustering
stages.note: MinHash/LSH signatures over the workspace corpus, family-level consensus

stages.name: Master merge
stages.note: Every JSON artefact produced so far folded into the master report skeleton

stages.name: ATT&CK mapping
stages.note: Observed techniques mapped to tactics, plus a Navigator JSON layer

stages.name: Campaign correlation
stages.note: Matched against the local campaign registry, auto-registered on a strong hit

phases.name: Report generation & retention
phases.aside: Stage 9 keeps the workspace from growing without bound: multi-gigabyte VMI memory dumps and raw eBPF event logs are purged according to the keep_vmi_memdump and keep_ebpf_raw flags in config.yaml.

stages.name: Report generation
stages.note: Master JSON consumed and compiled into a structured PDF executive summary

stages.name: Retention
stages.note: Intermediate artefact purge — VMI memory dumps, raw eBPF event logs
